examples.en: Charter flights carry relief supplies at cost under the emergency clause.
examples.zh: 依照紧急条款，包机「按成本」运送救援物资。

words.enDefinition: a systematic way of handling first cost

examples.en: Under the first cost method, replacement value never enters the books.
examples.zh: 采用「最初成本法」，重置价值永远不会进入账簿。

examples.en: The appraisal report compares the first cost method with current replacement pricing.
examples.zh: 评估报告把「最初成本法」与现行重置计价法作了对比。

words.enDefinition: stocks of spot

examples.en: Refiners draw on spot stocks whenever the pipeline from the Gulf is disrupted.
examples.zh: 一旦墨西哥湾的管道中断，炼厂就会动用「现货库存」。

examples.en: Spot stocks at the bonded warehouse rose sharply after the tariff announcement.
examples.zh: 关税消息公布后，保税仓库的「现货库存」大幅上升。

words.enDefinition: a paper concerning first-class commercial

examples.en: The treasury parks idle cash in first-class commercial paper maturing within ninety days.
examples.zh: 财务部门把闲置资金投到九十天内到期的「一等商业票据」上。

examples.en: Only issuers with strong ratings can place first-class commercial paper at tight spreads.
examples.zh: 只有评级优良的发行人才能以很窄的利差发行「一等商业票据」。

words.enDefinition: a schedule or sheet presenting standard job cost

examples.en: The workshop opens a standard job cost sheet the day the order is confirmed.
examples.zh: 订单确认当天，车间就开出一份「标准分批成本单」。

examples.en: Comparing two standard job cost sheets revealed the overtime hidden in finishing.
examples.zh: 对比两份「标准分批成本单」，发现了精加工环节隐藏的加班费。

collocations: prioritise the standard job cost sheet
standardise the standard job cost sheet
monitor the standard job cost sheet

words.zhGloss: 标准国际贸易商品分类
words.enDefinition: a classification for standard international trade
acceptedZhAnswers: 标准国际贸易商品分类

examples.en: Customs codes in the invoice must follow the standard international trade classification.
examples.zh: 发票上的海关编码必须遵循「标准国际贸易商品分类」。

examples.en: Statisticians regroup the standard international trade classification whenever new product families emerge.
examples.zh: 每当出现新的产品门类，统计人员就会调整「标准国际贸易商品分类」。

collocations: prioritise the standard international trade classification
standardise the standard international trade classification
monitor the standard international trade classification

words.enDefinition: a binding agreement concerning standard form

examples.en: The utility signs every installer on a standard form contract without negotiation.
examples.zh: 电力公司以「标准格式合同」签约每一家安装商，不接受讨价还价。

examples.en: Consumers rarely read the standard form contract printed on the back of the voucher.
examples.zh: 消费者很少去读印在凭证背面的「标准格式合同」。

words.enDefinition: amounts that must be paid or spent for standard fixed

examples.en: The budget locks standard fixed costs for rent and depreciation until June.
examples.zh: 预算把租金和折旧的「标准固定成本」锁定到六月。

examples.en: Spending variance analysis compares actual leases against standard fixed costs each quarter.
examples.zh: 支出差异分析每季度都会把实际租赁与「标准固定成本」对比。

words.enDefinition: amounts that must be paid or spent for standard

examples.en: The plant sets standard costs every autumn and holds them for twelve months.
examples.zh: 工厂每年秋天制定「标准成本」，十二个月内保持不变。

examples.en: Variance reports only make sense when standard costs reflect realistic output levels.
examples.zh: 只有当「标准成本」反映切实的产出水平时，差异报告才有意义。

words.enDefinition: reports produced under a standard costing system

examples.en: Managers skim standard costing reports before the Monday operations call.
examples.zh: 经理们在周一运营例会前会快速浏览「标准成本计算报告」。

examples.en: The assistant built standard costing reports with pivot tables instead of the old macros.
examples.zh: 助理用数据透视表替代旧宏，编制了「标准成本计算报告」。

words.enDefinition: a costing approach used for standard

examples.en: Standard costing works best where processes repeat and material usage is stable.
examples.zh: 在工序重复、用料稳定的环境里，「标准成本法」最为有效。

examples.en: We adopted standard costing to catch waste before the quarterly close.
examples.zh: 我们采用「标准成本计算」，以便在季度结账前发现浪费。

words.enDefinition: a system for standard cost

examples.en: Implementing a standard cost system took the factory nearly a full year.
examples.zh: 工厂实施「标准成本制度」花了将近整整一年。

examples.en: The consultant questioned whether a standard cost system still suits made-to-order work.
examples.zh: 顾问质疑「标准成本制度」是否仍适合按单定制类生产。

words.enDefinition: a schedule or sheet presenting standard cost

examples.en: The standard cost sheet lists film, glue, and carton for every SKU.
examples.zh: 「标准成本单」为每个单品列明膜材、胶水和纸箱。

examples.en: Revisions to the standard cost sheet require sign-off from plant control.
examples.zh: 「标准成本单」的修订必须经工厂控制部门签字批准。

words.enDefinition: a systematic way of handling standard cost

examples.en: Under the standard cost method, every intake is valued at plan, not at invoice.
examples.zh: 按「标准成本法」，每次入库都按计划价计值，而非发票价。

examples.en: The exam asked us to reconcile the standard cost method with actual pricing.
examples.zh: 考题要求我们把「标准成本法」与实际计价进行调节。

words.enDefinition: a card used for standard cost

examples.en: The quoting tool pulls the standard cost card straight from the ERP.
examples.zh: 报价工具直接从 ERP 调取「标准成本卡」。

examples.en: Anyone editing the standard cost card leaves an audit trail with a reason code.
examples.zh: 任何人修改「标准成本卡」都会留下带原因代码的审计痕迹。

words.enDefinition: a liability recognised for standard contract

examples.en: The penalty clause follows a standard contract provision used across the industry.
examples.zh: 违约金条款沿用了业界通行的「标准合同规定」。

examples.en: Counsel flagged a standard contract provision that conflicts with local labor law.
examples.zh: 法务指出一项与当地劳动法冲突的「标准合同规定」。

words.enDefinition: a binding agreement concerning standard

examples.en: Franchisees sign the standard contract without any right to redraw the fees.
examples.zh: 加盟商签署「标准合同」，无权重新议定费用。

examples.en: The standard contract caps liability at the price of the last shipment.
examples.zh: 「标准合同」把责任上限定在最近一批货的货款金额。

words.enDefinition: a planned amount of money set aside for standard

examples.en: Each store operates on a standard budget adjusted only for floor space.
examples.zh: 每家门店按「标准预算」运营，仅按营业面积作调整。

examples.en: The finance team rebuilt the standard budget after consolidating the two warehouses.
examples.zh: 合并两座仓库后，财务团队重编了「标准预算」。

words.enDefinition: the difference between planned and actual standard costs

examples.en: Standard costs variance reports arrive weekly, split by material, labor, and overhead.
examples.zh: 「标准成本差异」报告每周发布，按材料、人工和制造费用分列。

examples.en: A favorable standard costs variance hid the lower grade of tinplate we bought.
examples.zh: 有利的「标准成本差异」背后，是我们购入了等级更低的镀锡板。

words.enDefinition: the cost of depleted

examples.en: The mine's depleted cost dropped to zero once the final seam was worked out.
examples.zh: 最后一个矿层采完之后，这座矿的「耗余成本」降为零。

examples.en: Accountants track the depleted cost of each well against remaining certified reserves.
examples.zh: 会计按剩余探明储量跟踪每口井的「折耗后成本」。

words.enDefinition: management of staff

examples.en: In the classic org chart, staff management advises, while line management commands.
examples.zh: 在经典组织结构图中，「参谋管理」负责出谋划策，直线管理负责发号施令。

examples.en: Her role in staff management means she briefs the board but carries no budget.
examples.zh: 她担任的是「参谋管理」职能，向董事会作简报，但不掌握预算。

words.enDefinition: the cost of assumed

examples.en: The model's assumed cost of capital sits at eight percent, above the bank's offer.
examples.zh: 模型中的「假定资本成本」为百分之八，高于银行的报价。

examples.en: Bid teams flag any assumed cost that lacks a written supplier quote.
examples.zh: 投标团队会标记任何缺少供应商书面报价的「假定成本」。

words.enDefinition: stable production; a manufacturing method or production measure

examples.en: Rotating shifts through the furnace keeps stable production across the whole week.
examples.zh: 各班组轮流盯炉，保证了全周的「均衡生产」。

examples.en: Contracts with steel mills reward stable production schedules with better pricing.
examples.zh: 钢厂会给维持「稳定生产」节奏的客户更优惠的价格。

words.enDefinition: prices charged in stable transactions

examples.en: Shoppers return because the supermarket holds stable prices even during holidays.
examples.zh: 顾客愿意回头，是因为这家超市即使在节日期间也保持「稳定的价格」。

examples.en: Central bankers cite stable prices as the precondition for steady investment.
examples.zh: 央行官员把「物价稳定」视为投资平稳的前提条件。

words.enDefinition: a transfer of money made for stage

examples.en: The builder's stage payment schedule matches each milestone to a bank certificate.
examples.zh: 施工方的「阶段付款」计划把每个里程碑与银行证明挂钩。

examples.en: Clients delayed the second stage payment until the steel frame passed inspection.
examples.zh: 钢构架通过验收之前，客户推迟了第二笔「阶段付款」。

words.enDefinition: a deposit lodged with the treasury

examples.en: The municipality parks bond proceeds as a deposit at the treasury until tenders close.
examples.zh: 在招标结束之前，市政府把债券募集资金作为「金库存款」存放。

examples.en: Interest on the deposit at the treasury accrues monthly at the statutory rate.
examples.zh: 「金库存款」的利息按法定利率逐月累计。

words.enDefinition: a business entity associated with stock

examples.en: The family workshop became a stock company before the second plant opened.
examples.zh: 第二座工厂开建之前，家庭作坊改制成了「股份公司」。

examples.en: As a stock company, it must publish accounts whether shareholders like it or not.
examples.zh: 作为「股份公司」，无论股东乐意与否，它都必须公布账目。

words.enDefinition: a corporation engaged in stock clearing

examples.en: The stock clearing corporation settles trades within two business days.
examples.zh: 这家「股份清算公司」在两个营业日内完成交易结算。

examples.en: Brokers fund their margin accounts daily at the stock clearing corporation.
examples.zh: 券商每天都要向「股份清算公司」存入保证金。

words.enDefinition: the net amount remaining for stock

examples.en: The cycle count reconciled the stock balance with the warehouse system overnight.
examples.zh: 循环盘点连夜把「库存余额」与仓储系统核对一致。

examples.en: A negative stock balance on the report usually means a missed goods receipt.
examples.zh: 报表上出现负的「库存余额」，通常意味着漏记了一张收货单。

words.enDefinition: explanatory disclosures related to stock debit

examples.en: Stores issue stock debit notes whenever finished goods arrive from the plant.
examples.zh: 成品一到厂，门店就开具「货物收入凭单」。

examples.en: The audit sampled twenty stock debit notes against signed delivery dockets.
examples.zh: 审计人员抽取二十张「货物收入凭单」与签收单核对。

words.enDefinition: stock held in storage

examples.en: Insurance covers stock in storage up to the declared ceiling each month.
examples.zh: 保险按每月申报的上限承保「库存物资」。

examples.en: Humidity ruined part of the stock in storage during the monsoon week.
examples.zh: 雨季那一周，湿气损毁了部分「库存物资」。

words.enDefinition: the cost of assessed program

examples.en: Each member state's assessed program cost follows the agreed UN scale.
examples.zh: 各成员国的「摊派计划费用」按照议定的联合国分摊比额表确定。

examples.en: Delinquent payments on the assessed program cost triggered voting suspension.
examples.zh: 拖欠「摊派计划费用」触动了表决权的暂停机制。

words.enDefinition: a planned amount of money set aside for assessed

examples.en: The assessed budget for peacekeeping rose three percent this financial year.
examples.zh: 本财政年度维和「摊派预算」上调了百分之三。

examples.en: Committee members argued over the assessed budget line for training missions.
examples.zh: 委员会成员为培训任务的「摊派预算」科目争论不休。

words.enDefinition: to evaluate opportunities in a market

examples.en: Before patenting the dispenser, we hired consultants to assess market opportunities.
examples.zh: 为分配器申请专利之前，我们聘请顾问「评估市场机会」。

examples.en: Teams that fail to assess market opportunities often chase the loudest customer.
examples.zh: 不善于「判断市场机会」的团队，往往只会追着嗓门最大的客户跑。

words.zhGloss: (海关发给的)底货装载许可证
words.enDefinition: a document authorising the stuffing (loading) of cargo into a container, often for customs or terminal control
acceptedZhAnswers: (海关发给的)底货装载许可证

examples.en: The terminal will not load the container without a valid stuffing order.
examples.zh: 没有有效的「底货装载许可证」，码头不会为集装箱装货。

examples.en: Customs issued the stuffing order only after inspecting the declared pallet count.
examples.zh: 海关核实申报的托盘数量后，才签发这份「装货许可证」。

words.enDefinition: the price charged in stiff transactions

examples.en: The boutique charged a stiff price for shoes we later saw at the outlet.
examples.zh: 精品店为那双鞋开出了「昂贵的价格」，后来我们在折扣店看到了同款。

examples.en: Vendors quote a stiff price whenever the buyer's tender names only one brand.
examples.zh: 只要买方的招标只指定一个品牌，供应商就会报出「高昂的价格」。

words.enDefinition: the price charged in sticky transactions

examples.en: Menu reprinting costs explain why restaurant prices are a classic sticky price.
examples.zh: 重印菜单的成本解释了为什么餐馆价格是典型的「粘性价格」。

examples.en: In a recession, the sticky price of labor keeps firms from cutting wages quickly.
examples.zh: 衰退期工资这种「粘性价格」使企业难以快速降薪。

words.enDefinition: orders related to assembly production

examples.en: The scheduler releases assembly production orders only after kits pass the check.
examples.zh: 只有成套件通过核查后，排产员才下达「装配生产工作单」。

examples.en: Two assembly production orders collided on the same line last Friday.
examples.zh: 上周五，两张「装配生产工作单」在同一条生产线上撞了车。

words.enDefinition: a system for assembly cost

examples.en: The assembly cost system charges each workstation for its labor minutes.
examples.zh: 「装配成本制度」按工位归集人工分钟数。

examples.en: Under the assembly cost system, missing fasteners show up as unfavorable material variance.
examples.zh: 在「装配成本制度」下，紧固件缺失会体现为不利的材料差异。

words.enDefinition: the cost of assembly

examples.en: Moving the harness build in-house cut assembly cost per unit by nine percent.
examples.zh: 把线束制造收归厂内，使每台的「装配成本」降低了百分之九。

examples.en: Buyers push suppliers to quote assembly cost separately from parts.
examples.zh: 买方要求供应商把「装配成本」与零件价格分开报价。

words.enDefinition: assembling production; a manufacturing method or production measure

examples.en: Assembling production happens at the Satu Mare plant, while stamping stays in Korea.
examples.zh: 「装配生产」放在萨图马雷工厂进行，冲压工序则留在韩国。

examples.en: The apprenticeship covers assembling production, quality checks, and basic maintenance.
examples.zh: 学徒课程涵盖「装配生产」、质量检验和基础维护。

words.enDefinition: meeting for stockholders'

examples.en: The chairman opened the stockholders' meeting with a frank apology for the delay.
examples.zh: 董事长在「股东大会」上以坦诚的道歉作为开场，回应这次延误。

examples.en: Proxy advisors urged holders to attend the stockholders' meeting in person.
examples.zh: 代理顾问敦促股东亲自出席「股东大会」。

words.enDefinition: a stoppage of payment used in professional practice

examples.en: The bank's stoppage of payment froze every transfer out of the escrow account.
examples.zh: 银行的「停止支付」措施冻结了托管账户的全部对外转账。

examples.en: Suppliers learned of the stoppage of payment only after their invoices bounced.
examples.zh: 供应商是在发票遭退票后，才知道公司已「停止支付」。

words.enDefinition: a notice concerning stop-payment

examples.en: She lodged a stop-payment notice with the bank the same afternoon.
examples.zh: 当天下午她就在银行提交了「停止支付通知书」。

examples.en: A stop-payment notice protects the payer only until the cheque expires.
examples.zh: 「止付通知」只在支票有效期内为付款人提供保护。

words.enDefinition: a securities trading order of the stop limit type

examples.en: She placed a stop limit order to exit the trade near forty-two euros.
examples.zh: 她设置了一笔「止损限价指令」，打算在四十二欧元附近离场。

examples.en: The stop limit order triggered in the morning gap but filled far lower.
examples.zh: 「止损限价指令」在早盘跳空时触发，成交价却低得多。

words.enDefinition: a situation where stock is unavailable

examples.en: Frequent stock out events on vitamins pushed regulars to the pharmacy next door.
examples.zh: 维生素频繁「断货」，把常客都推到了隔壁药房。

examples.en: The dashboard flags any stock out longer than twenty-four hours.
examples.zh: 看板会标记任何超过二十四小时的「缺货」。

words.enDefinition: a stock of materials held for use or sale

examples.en: The warehouse holds a stock of material sufficient for six production weeks.
examples.zh: 仓库备有足够六周生产的「材料库存」。

examples.en: Auditors questioned the growing stock of material during a demand slump.
examples.zh: 需求低迷之际，审计人员对不断膨胀的「材料库存」提出质疑。

words.enDefinition: a clerk responsible for stock record

examples.en: The stock record clerk reconciles every goods issue against signed requisitions.
examples.zh: 「库存品收发员」将每笔领料与签字的申请单核对。

examples.en: At her retirement party, we learned the stock record clerk had never taken leave.
examples.zh: 退休欢送会上我们才知道，这位「库存品收发员」从未休过假。

collocations: close out the stock record clerk

words.enDefinition: a document presenting information about stockholders annual

examples.en: The stockholders annual report reached mailboxes a week before the vote.
examples.zh: 「股东年度报表」在表决前一周寄到了股东信箱。

examples.en: Designers rebuilt the stockholders annual report with clearer cash flow charts.
examples.zh: 设计师重做了「股东年度报表」，现金流量图更清晰了。

words.enDefinition: a right belonging to a stockholder

examples.en: Preemption is a stockholder's right that survives any change of control.
examples.zh: 优先认购是随控股权变更依然存续的一项「股东权利」。

examples.en: The charter spells out every stockholder's right in plain language now.
examples.zh: 如今公司章程用平实的语言写明了每一项「股东权利」。

words.enDefinition: an accepted requirement for stockholder's purchasing power

examples.en: The utility discloses a stockholder's purchasing power standard in its consumer charter.
examples.zh: 这家公用事业公司在客户章程中披露了「股东购买力标准」。

examples.en: Dividend policy now references the stockholder's purchasing power standard after inflation.
examples.zh: 考虑通胀因素后，股利政策开始参照「股东购买力标准」。

collocations: prioritise the stockholder's purchasing power standard
standardise the stockholder's purchasing power standard
monitor the stockholder's purchasing power standard

words.enDefinition: the stockholder recorded as owner on the company’s books

examples.en: Only a stockholder of record on June 1 receives the special dividend.
examples.zh: 只有六月一日的「在册股东」才能获得这笔特别股利。

examples.en: Beneficial owners differ from a stockholder of record in how votes reach the company.
examples.zh: 受益所有人与「登记在册的股东」在表决权传递方式上有所不同。

words.enDefinition: a listed schedule of stockholder

examples.en: The proxy fight began the day the stockholder list was finalized.
examples.zh: 「股东名册」定稿当天，代理权之争就拉开了序幕。

examples.en: Under police supervision, inspectors copied the entire stockholder list for the probe.
examples.zh: 在警方监督下，调查人员复制了整份「股东登记表」用于调查。

words.enDefinition: the cost of stock-out

examples.en: Planners weigh the stock-out cost against the carrying cost of deeper shelves.
examples.zh: 计划员要在「缺货成本」与加深货架的持有成本之间权衡。

examples.en: After the holiday stock-out cost hit margins, we widened the safety buffer.
examples.zh: 节日「缺货成本」侵蚀毛利之后，我们扩大了安全库存。

words.enDefinition: a statistics of trade used in professional practice

examples.en: Customs published the statistics of trade three weeks late again.
examples.zh: 海关的「贸易统计」又晚发布了三个星期。

examples.en: Her thesis disputes the official statistics of trade for re-export flows.
examples.zh: 她的论文质疑官方「贸易统计」中对转口流量的记录。

words.enDefinition: a process or check used to manage statistical stock

examples.en: Statistical stock control flags any item whose demand suddenly turns erratic.
examples.zh: 「统计性库存控制」会标记任何需求突然变得反常的物料。

examples.en: The workshop introduced statistical stock control to the spare-parts storeroom.
examples.zh: 车间在备件库房引入了「统计库存控制」。

words.enDefinition: a deposit for security used in professional practice

examples.en: The tenant paid a deposit for security equal to three months' rent.
examples.zh: 租户缴纳了相当于三个月租金的「保证金」。

examples.en: Bidders forfeit their deposit for security if they withdraw after the shortlist.
examples.zh: 入围后撤标的投标方将被没收「保证金」。

words.enDefinition: the cost of static standard

examples.en: The plant froze a static standard cost for copper despite the commodity rally.
examples.zh: 尽管大宗商品行情大涨，工厂对铜仍维持「静态标准成本」。

examples.en: Comparing actuals with a static standard cost exaggerates variances in volatile years.
examples.zh: 行情剧烈的年份，用「静态标准成本」去比实际数会放大差异。

words.enDefinition: a planned amount of money set aside for static

examples.en: The council adopts a static budget and holds departments to it rigidly.
examples.zh: 委员会采用「静态预算」，各部门必须严格执行。

examples.en: A static budget ignores volume swings, so monthly variances look alarming.
examples.zh: 「静态预算」不考虑产量波动，因此月度差异看起来总很吓人。

words.enDefinition: statement of sales used in professional practice

examples.en: The branch emails a statement of sales to head office every Friday.
examples.zh: 分店每周五向总部电邮一份「销售报告表」。

examples.en: Bank lenders asked for a statement of sales covering the last four quarters.
examples.zh: 银行放贷方要求提供最近四个季度的「销售报告表」。

words.enDefinition: transfer of rights under a throughput processing contract

examples.en: Bankers refused the loan until the assignment of throughput contracts was notarized.
examples.zh: 「加工合同转让」完成公证之后，银行才同意放贷。

examples.en: The assignment of throughput contracts lets the new operator keep the refinery running.
examples.zh: 「转让加工合同」使新运营商得以维持炼厂运转。

collocations: negotiate the assignment of throughput contracts
renew the assignment of throughput contracts
terminate the assignment of throughput contracts

words.enDefinition: an assignment of interest used in professional practice

examples.en: Her assignment of interest in the partnership took effect on the first of May.
examples.zh: 她的「合伙权益转让」于五月一日生效。

examples.en: Lenders demand notice of any assignment of interest within ten days.
examples.zh: 放贷方要求任何「权益转让」都须在十天内通知他们。

words.enDefinition: deposit that has been paid

examples.en: The deposit paid to the auction house shows as a receivable until settlement.
examples.zh: 付给拍卖行的「存出保证金」在结算前挂账为应收款。

examples.en: We recorded the deposit paid for the crane rental under prepayments.
examples.zh: 吊车租赁的「已付保证金」记在预付款项科目下。

words.enDefinition: the cost of steam

examples.en: Steam cost per tonne climbed when the gas contract reset in October.
examples.zh: 十月天然气合同重签后，每吨「蒸汽成本」上升了。

examples.en: Insulating the headers cut the steam cost more than the engineer predicted.
examples.zh: 给集箱加保温层后，「蒸汽成本」的降幅超出工程师的预期。

words.enDefinition: a deposit received as security for guarantees

examples.en: The ledger shows deposit received for guarantees from three franchise partners.
examples.zh: 账上显示已收到三家加盟伙伴的「保证金」。

examples.en: Deposit received for guarantees stays in escrow until the lease expires.
examples.zh: 「已收保证金」将存放托管账户，直至租约到期。

words.enDefinition: the cost of step-variable

examples.en: Quality inspectors make wages a step-variable cost, flat until volume jumps a range.
examples.zh: 质检员工资属于「阶梯式变动成本」，产量不出区间就保持平稳。

examples.en: The model treats overtime as a step-variable cost that appears after ninety percent load.
examples.zh: 模型把加班费视为「阶梯式变动成本」，负载超过九成才出现。

words.enDefinition: amounts that must be paid or spent for step-variable capacity

examples.en: Adding a second oven line introduces step-variable capacity costs rather than smooth increases.
examples.zh: 增建第二条烤炉线带来的是「阶梯式产能成本」，而非平滑的增长。

examples.en: Finance plots step-variable capacity costs so expansion requests carry visible jumps.
examples.zh: 财务把「阶梯式产能成本」画成图，让扩产申请中的跳增一目了然。

words.enDefinition: amounts that must be paid or spent for step

examples.en: Each new delivery route adds a truck and driver, a textbook case of step costs.
examples.zh: 每新增一条配送线路就要添一辆车和一名司机，是「阶梯成本」的教科书案例。

examples.en: Rent jumps the moment we lease the annex, so storage behaves like step costs.
examples.zh: 一租下附属仓库，租金就跳一档，仓储开支因此呈现「阶梯成本」特征。

words.enDefinition: a bank’s conditional undertaking to pay a beneficiary when stipulated documents are presented (letter of credit)

examples.en: The supplier accepted an assignable credit so it could pass part to its mill.
examples.zh: 供应商接受了「可转让信用证」，以便把部分金额转让给其工厂。

examples.en: Banks charge a transfer fee when an assignable credit moves to a second beneficiary.
examples.zh: 「可转让信用证」转给第二受益人时，银行会收取转让费。

words.enDefinition: a revaluation for assets

examples.en: The interim statements absorbed an assets revaluation triggered by the land rezoning.
examples.zh: 土地改划触发「资产重估」，中期报表已将其计入。

examples.en: Independent valuers handled the assets revaluation for the annual report.
examples.zh: 年报的「资产重估」由独立估值师完成。

words.enDefinition: a planned amount of money set aside for flexible standard

examples.en: The plant adopted a flexible standard budget that flexes with kiln utilization.
examples.zh: 工厂采用了随窑炉利用率伸缩的「弹性标准预算」。

examples.en: A flexible standard budget keeps variances meaningful when volumes swing.
examples.zh: 产量波动时，「弹性标准预算」能让差异分析依然有意义。

words.enDefinition: a line of automatic production

examples.en: The new automatic production line assembled switches with barely six operators.
examples.zh: 新的「自动生产线」装配开关，只需六名左右的操作工。

examples.en: A jam in the automatic production line halted orders for half a day.
examples.zh: 「自动生产线」一次卡料让订单停了半天。

words.enDefinition: a market for sold out

examples.en: The importer reported a sold out market for hand warmers until February.
examples.zh: 进口商报告说，暖手宝市场「已经售罄」，要到二月才有货。

examples.en: Dealers face a sold out market, so secondhand premiums keep climbing.
examples.zh: 经销商面临「售罄的市场」，二手溢价因此持续走高。

words.enDefinition: an order related to sold on

examples.en: The furniture workshop works sold on order, so nothing sits in a showroom.
examples.zh: 这家家具作坊采取「按订单销售」模式，展厅从不压货。

examples.en: Bakes are sold on order only, never from a counter display.
examples.zh: 面包只按「预订销售」，从不摆柜台现货。

words.enDefinition: a market for soft

examples.en: Charter rates sag in a soft market, so owners postpone deliveries.
examples.zh: 「市场疲软」时租船费率走低，船东纷纷推迟交船。

examples.en: Even in a soft market, the boutique holds its price discipline.
examples.zh: 即便身处「不景气的市场」，这家精品店依然坚守价格纪律。

collocations: clear goods through the soft market

words.enDefinition: a quota for autonomous export

examples.en: The association set an autonomous export quota of two million units this year.
examples.zh: 行业协会今年自定了二百万件的「自动出口限额」。

examples.en: Compliance with the autonomous export quota spared the industry a formal tariff.
examples.zh: 遵守「自动出口限额」使该行业免遭正式关税。

collocations: comply with the autonomous export quota

words.enDefinition: a source of revenue used in professional practice

examples.en: Subscriptions became the studio's steadiest source of revenue last year.
examples.zh: 去年，订阅成了这家工作室最稳定的「收入来源」。

examples.en: The charity diversifies each source of revenue before the grant cycle ends.
examples.zh: 在拨款周期结束前，这家慈善机构为每一项「收入来源」做多元化布局。

words.enDefinition: yield earned from flat

examples.en: The gilt's flat yield ignores any gain or loss at maturity.
examples.zh: 这只金边债券的「平价收益率」不考虑到期时的损益。

examples.en: Analysts quote the flat yield by dividing the coupon by the clean price.
examples.zh: 分析师用票息除以除权价来计算「平价收益率」。

words.enDefinition: the price charged in flat transactions

examples.en: The airline charged a flat price for any bag under twenty kilograms.
examples.zh: 航空公司对二十公斤以下的行李一律收取「统一价格」。

examples.en: Subscribers prefer a flat price to per-ride charges that change monthly.
examples.zh: 订阅者更喜欢「一口价」，而不是逐月变动的按次计费。

words.enDefinition: prices charged in flat list transactions

examples.en: The hardware chain publishes flat list prices so branches stop improvising discounts.
examples.zh: 五金连锁店公布「统一价格表」，各分店不再随意打折。

examples.en: Buyers negotiate from flat list prices printed in the annual catalogue.
examples.zh: 买方以年度目录印制的「统一价目」为基准展开谈判。

words.enDefinition: the cost of flat

examples.en: The caterer charges a flat cost per head, drinks included.
examples.zh: 承办宴席的公司按人头收取「统一成本价」，酒水包含在内。

examples.en: Shipping under the contract runs at a flat cost regardless of distance.
examples.zh: 合同项下的运输按「统一成本」计费，与距离无关。

words.enDefinition: a fee or commission paid in respect of flat

examples.en: The agent charges a flat commission of two percent on every charter.
examples.zh: 代理对每份租船合同统一收取百分之二的「固定佣金」。

examples.en: A flat commission simplifies billing but can overcharge small consignments.
examples.zh: 「统一手续费」简化了账单，却可能让小批量货物多付钱。

words.enDefinition: quality measures for sound

examples.en: The inspector passed the drums because each met sound quality standards.
examples.zh: 检验员放行了这批桶件，因为每一件都达到「完好质量」标准。

examples.en: Buyers may reject any lot that fails to show sound quality on arrival.
examples.zh: 凡到货时不能证明「质量完好」的批次，买方均可拒收。

words.enDefinition: a planned amount of money set aside for departmental

examples.en: Marketing blew its departmental budget on the failed festival sponsorship.
examples.zh: 市场部把「部门预算」都砸在了失败的音乐节赞助上。

examples.en: Each January, department heads defend their departmental budget before the CFO.
examples.zh: 每年一月，各部门主管都要向首席财务官为「分部预算」作辩护。

words.enDefinition: a systematic way of handling flexible budgets

examples.en: The flexible budgets method lets the plant absorb demand swings without new approvals.
examples.zh: 「弹性预算法」让工厂无需重新审批就能消化需求波动。

examples.en: Students practice the flexible budgets method on a case about a bakery chain.
examples.zh: 学生们通过一家连锁面包房的案例练习「弹性预算法」。

words.enDefinition: a process or check used to manage flexible budgetary

examples.en: Flexible budgetary control adjusts spending caps as the order book changes.
examples.zh: 「弹性预算控制」会随订单簿的变化调整支出上限。

examples.en: Under flexible budgetary control, the unit cost target moves with output.
examples.zh: 在「弹性预算控制」下，单位成本目标随产量联动。

words.enDefinition: an amount deducted or set aside for flexible budget

examples.en: The flexible budget allowance for utilities rises four percent per thousand units.
examples.zh: 水电的「弹性预算限额」每千件产品上调百分之四。

examples.en: Supervisors compare hours worked with the flexible budget allowance before overtime approval.
examples.zh: 批准加班之前，主管会把实际工时与「弹性预算限额」比对。

words.enDefinition: the ability of prices to adjust to market conditions

examples.en: The monopoly's flexibility of prices lets it pass fuel costs straight to users.
examples.zh: 垄断企业的「价格弹性」使它能把燃料成本直接转嫁给用户。

examples.en: Economists measure the flexibility of prices by watching how quickly quotes adjust.
examples.zh: 经济学家观察报价调整的快慢来衡量「价格弹性」。

words.enDefinition: management of department of industrial

examples.en: She lectures in the department of industrial management twice a week.
examples.zh: 她每周在「工业管理系」讲授两次课。

examples.en: The department of industrial management partnered with the rail freight operator for internships.
examples.zh: 「工业管理系」与铁路货运运营商建立了实习合作。

words.enDefinition: a planned amount of money set aside for department

examples.en: Maintenance stayed inside its department budget despite the emergency pump repair.
examples.zh: 尽管水泵紧急维修，维修部仍守住了「部门预算」。

examples.en: Any overage on the department budget needs a written explanation within five days.
examples.zh: 「部门预算」一旦超支，五天内必须提交书面说明。

words.enDefinition: a department of cost used in professional practice

examples.en: The department of cost issues the monthly absorption rates to every plant.
examples.zh: 「成本部门」每月向各厂发布分摊率。

examples.en: Queries about the new charging scheme go straight to the department of cost.
examples.zh: 关于新分摊办法的疑问，请直接咨询「成本部门」。

words.enDefinition: movement of prices up and down over time

examples.en: The grain desk logs every fluctuation of prices above two percent in a day.
examples.zh: 粮食交易台会把单日超过百分之二的「价格涨落」都记录下来。

examples.en: Retailers smooth the fluctuation of prices with quarterly forward purchases.
examples.zh: 零售商通过按季度远期采购来平滑「价格的波动」。

words.enDefinition: flow of costs used in professional practice

examples.en: The diagram traces the flow of costs from raw wool to finished blanket.
examples.zh: 这张图追溯了从原毛到成品毯的「成本流转」。

examples.en: Auditors tested the flow of costs through all three workshops.
examples.zh: 审计人员对三个车间的「成本流转」进行了穿行测试。

words.enDefinition: flow line production; a manufacturing method or production measure

examples.en: Flow line production doubled output once the paint booth stopped bottlenecking.
examples.zh: 喷漆房不再卡壳之后，「流水线生产」的产量翻了一番。

examples.en: Textbooks contrast flow line production with job shops built for one-offs.
examples.zh: 教科书把「流水线生产」与专做单件的机群式车间进行对比。

words.enDefinition: a costing approach used for average

examples.en: Under average costing, each goods receipt re-prices the entire balance.
examples.zh: 在「平均成本计算」下，每次收货都会重新计算全部结存的单价。

examples.en: Average costing spared the team the batch-by-batch price chasing that FIFO requires.
examples.zh: 「平均成本法」省去了先进先出法逐批追价的麻烦。

words.enDefinition: a unit of average cost per

examples.en: Lunchboxes shipped in August pushed average cost per unit to a new low.
examples.zh: 八月发货的餐盒使「单位平均成本」降至新低。

examples.en: CFOs track average cost per unit weekly during ramp-up quarters.
examples.zh: 爬坡季度的「单位平均成本」，首席财务官会每周跟踪。

words.enDefinition: a systematic way of handling average cost

examples.en: The warehouse values fuel with the average cost method, refreshed on each delivery.
examples.zh: 仓库对燃油采用「平均成本法」计值，每次到货后更新。

examples.en: Tax authorities accepted the average cost method for the scrap-metal inventory.
examples.zh: 税务机关认可对废金属存货采用「平均成本法」。

words.enDefinition: a curve showing the relationship for average cost

examples.en: The average cost curve bottoms out at around eight thousand units a month.
examples.zh: 「平均成本曲线」在月产八千件左右触底。

examples.en: Drawing the average cost curve helped the class see where economies of scale end.
examples.zh: 画出「平均成本曲线」后，同学们看清了规模经济的尽头在哪里。

words.enDefinition: the cost of output on an average basis

examples.en: Average cost per meal fell once the kitchen standardized its prep.
examples.zh: 厨房实现备料标准化后，每餐的「平均成本」下降了。

examples.en: Pricing below average cost is sustainable only while cash reserves last.
examples.zh: 只有在现金储备允许的情况下，按低于「平均成本」的价格销售才可持续。

words.enDefinition: a curve showing the relationship for average fixed cost

examples.en: The average fixed cost curve falls forever, approaching but never touching zero.
examples.zh: 「平均固定成本曲线」不断下降，趋近却永远到不了零。

examples.en: Tutors overlay the average fixed cost curve on the variable curve to build the total.
examples.zh: 辅导老师把「平均固定成本曲线」叠加在变动成本曲线上，合成总成本。

words.enDefinition: the cost of average fixed

examples.en: Spreading rent over more tablets lowered our average fixed cost per unit.
examples.zh: 把租金摊到更多台设备上，我们每台的「平均固定成本」降低了。

examples.en: Average fixed cost never decides pricing on its own, the consultant warned.
examples.zh: 顾问提醒，「平均固定成本」本身不能单独决定定价。

words.enDefinition: retailing for small scale

examples.en: Small scale retailing survives in villages where supermarkets cannot justify a store.
examples.zh: 在超市觉得不值得设店的村庄，「小规模零售」得以生存。

examples.en: Her thesis on small scale retailing interviewed forty kiosk owners.
examples.zh: 她的「小规模零售」论文访谈了四十位报刊亭主。

words.enDefinition: the price charged in demand transactions

examples.en: At the demand price of nine dollars, only half the harvest finds buyers.
examples.zh: 在九美元的「需求价格」下，只有一半收成能找到买家。

examples.en: The auction stopped when bidding passed the demand price buyers had signaled.
examples.zh: 竞价超过买方暗示的「需求价格」后，拍卖便告中止。

words.enDefinition: the price charged in average transactions

examples.en: The dashboard reports the average price paid per tonne across all grades.
examples.zh: 看板显示所有品级每吨的「平均价格」。

examples.en: Our average price for the season sits four percent below last year's.
examples.zh: 本季的「平均价格」比去年低百分之四。

words.enDefinition: trade activity concerning floating

examples.en: Floating trade through the strait picked up once the convoy escorts arrived.
examples.zh: 护航船队到位后，经海峡的「海上贸易」逐渐恢复。

examples.en: Archives describe the floating trade that linked the islands for centuries.
examples.zh: 档案记载了几个世纪以来联结各岛屿的「海上贸易」。

words.enDefinition: the cost of social opportunity

examples.en: The dam's social opportunity cost includes the farmland the reservoir will drown.
examples.zh: 这座大坝的「社会机会成本」包括水库将淹没的农田。

examples.en: Economists price a highway project by its social opportunity cost, not just its budget.
examples.zh: 经济学家按「社会机会成本」而非仅按预算来评价公路项目。

words.enDefinition: a marketing concept focused on social objectives

examples.en: Under the social marketing concept, the firm weighs profit, wants, and public wellbeing.
examples.zh: 按照「社会营销观念」，企业要兼顾利润、需求与公众福祉。

examples.en: Her campaign for the water utility embodies the social marketing concept.
examples.zh: 她为自来水公司策划的宣传活动体现了「社会营销观念」。

words.enDefinition: the cost of auxiliary department

examples.en: The maintenance shop's auxiliary department cost is charged out by labor hour.
examples.zh: 维修车间的「辅助部门成本」按工时对外分摊。

examples.en: Recharging auxiliary department cost fairly required a fresh activity study.
examples.zh: 要公平分摊「辅助部门成本」，就得重新做一次作业研究。

words.enDefinition: financial gain arising from available

examples.en: Only available profit after tax distributions may fund the community hall.
examples.zh: 只有缴税分红后的「可用利润」才能用于修建社区礼堂。

examples.en: The loan covenant tests available profit rather than headline earnings each quarter.
examples.zh: 该契约条款考核的是「可用利润」，而不是报表利润。

words.enDefinition: inventory (stock) of available from held for sale or use

examples.en: The catalog marks every valve available from stock for next-day dispatch.
examples.zh: 产品目录标明每种阀门都「仓库有现货」，可次日发运。

examples.en: Only half the ordered lengths are available from stock this week.
examples.zh: 本周订购的长度规格只有一半「仓库有现货」。

words.enDefinition: a planned amount of money set aside for auxiliary unit

examples.en: The training center submits its auxiliary unit budget with the group plan.
examples.zh: 培训中心把「附属单位预算」随集团计划一并上报。

examples.en: Cuts to the auxiliary unit budget delayed the canteen renovation.
examples.zh: 「附属单位预算」遭削减后，食堂翻新被迫推迟。

words.enDefinition: management of democratic

examples.en: The co-op practices democratic management, one member one vote on big spending.
examples.zh: 这家合作社实行「民主管理」，重大开支一人一票。

examples.en: Democratic management slows decisions at times but keeps the workshop fiercely loyal.
examples.zh: 「民主管理」虽然拖慢决策，却留住了车间的人心。

words.enDefinition: the cost of attributable

examples.en: Each course carries only its attributable cost, never shared overhead.
examples.zh: 每门课程只计其「可归属成本」，从不摊入公共间接费。

examples.en: Grant rules say only attributable cost is eligible for reimbursement.
examples.zh: 资助规则规定，只有「可归属成本」才能报销。

words.enDefinition: the amount of money charged or quoted for fixed resale

examples.en: Imposing a fixed resale price on dealers breached the competition rules.
examples.zh: 对经销商强制执行「固定转售价格」违反了竞争规则。

examples.en: Suppliers may recommend prices but cannot enforce a fixed resale price.
examples.zh: 供应商可以建议零售价，但不得强制「固定转售价格」。

words.enDefinition: a fixed ratio of inputs to output in production

examples.en: The recipe assumes a fixed production coefficient of three kilos of brine per casing.
examples.zh: 配方假定每副肠衣用三公斤盐水这一「固定生产系数」。

examples.en: Input-output tables rely on a fixed production coefficient for each sector.
examples.zh: 投入产出表假定每个部门都有「固定的生产系数」。

words.enDefinition: the price charged in fixed transactions

examples.en: The renovation quote is a fixed price, so surprises land on the builder.
examples.zh: 装修报价是「固定价格」，意外情况也包含在内。

examples.en: Contracts at a fixed price protect buyers when commodity markets turn wild.
examples.zh: 大宗商品市场剧烈波动时，「固定价格」合同能保护买方。

words.enDefinition: a pool of fixed cost

examples.en: The controller lumps rent, rates, and security into one fixed cost pool.
examples.zh: 主计长把租金、房产税和保安费归入同一个「固定成本库」。

examples.en: Each fixed cost pool carries its own allocation basis in the model.
examples.zh: 模型中每个「固定成本类」都有各自的分摊基础。

words.enDefinition: budgets that do not vary with activity level

examples.en: Fixed budgets ignore demand shifts, so quarterly reviews feel unfair to sales.
examples.zh: 「固定预算」无视需求变化，季度考核让销售团队觉得不公。

examples.en: The group still runs fixed budgets because investors value predictability.
examples.zh: 集团仍沿用「固定预算」，因为投资者看重可预测性。

words.enDefinition: a market for auction

examples.en: The flower auction market opens at four in the morning for wholesalers.
examples.zh: 面向批发商的「拍卖市场」凌晨四点开市。

examples.en: Fine art prices are discovered in the auction market, not in shops.
examples.zh: 艺术品的价格是在「拍卖市场」发现的，而不是在店铺里。

words.enDefinition: speculative production; a manufacturing method or production measure

examples.en: Committing to speculative production before the fair risked half the season's cash.
examples.zh: 在展会之前就「冒险投产」，押上了半个季度的现金。

examples.en: The vineyard avoids speculative production, bottling only after orders clear.
examples.zh: 这家葡萄园不做「投机性生产」，订单确认后才灌装。

words.enDefinition: a market for speculative

examples.en: Traders pulled out of the speculative market the moment the futures curve inverted.
examples.zh: 期货曲线一倒挂，交易员便撤离了这个「投机市场」。

examples.en: Fresh copper supplies calmed the speculative market within two weeks.
examples.zh: 新增的铜供应让「投机市场」在两周内平静下来。

words.enDefinition: a market for speculation

examples.en: Regulators warn that coin grading has become a speculation market.
examples.zh: 监管机构提醒，钱币评级已经变成了「投机市场」。

examples.en: The speculation market in parking spaces collapsed once the city built garages.
examples.zh: 市政府建起车库后，车位「投机市场」应声崩塌。

words.enDefinition: amounts that must be paid or spent for specified

examples.en: The grant covers only the specified costs listed in Annex Two.
examples.zh: 资助只覆盖附件二中列明的「规定费用」。

examples.en: Invoices outside the specified costs get rejected by the program office automatically.
examples.zh: 超出「规定费用」的发票会被项目办公室自动退回。

words.enDefinition: the cost of specification

examples.en: Adding the extra coating raised the specification cost of every panel.
examples.zh: 增加额外涂层提高了每块板材的「规定成本」。

examples.en: The tender compares bids against the specification cost prepared by engineering.
examples.zh: 评标时以工程部编制的「规定成本」作为比价依据。

words.enDefinition: a system for specific-order cost

examples.en: Under the specific-order cost system, each yacht carries its own job number.
examples.zh: 在「分批成本制度」下，每艘游艇都有自己的工单号。

examples.en: The specific-order cost system traces designer changes straight into the job file.
examples.zh: 「分批（定单）成本制度」把设计变更直接计入对应工单。

words.enDefinition: fixed-term loans that are unsecured

examples.en: The bank books fixed loans unsecured to longtime customers at preferential rates.
examples.zh: 银行以优惠利率向老客户发放「定期信用放款」。

examples.en: Their portfolio mixes mortgages with fixed loans unsecured on a three-year term.
examples.zh: 他们的资产组合把按揭与三年期的「定期信用放款」搭配在一起。

words.enDefinition: amounts that must be paid or spent for fixed

examples.en: Fixed costs barely moved even after we closed the second showroom.
examples.zh: 关闭第二家展厅后，「固定成本」几乎没有变化。

examples.en: Airlines battle their fixed costs with every extra seat sold at the margin.
examples.zh: 航空公司靠加卖的每一个座位来对抗高昂的「固定成本」。

words.enDefinition: the price charged in spot transactions

examples.en: Buyers settled the cargo at the spot price quoted on the day of arrival.
examples.zh: 货物按到港当日报出的「现货价格」结算。

examples.en: The spot price for gas doubled within a week of the outage.
examples.zh: 断供发生后一周内，天然气的「现货价格」翻了一番。

words.enDefinition: a market for immediate delivery and payment rather than future settlement

examples.en: Refiners top up volumes on the spot market when the pipeline halts.
examples.zh: 管道停输时，炼厂会在「现货市场」补足货量。

examples.en: Producers prefer annual contracts, but the spot market keeps everyone honest.
examples.zh: 生产商偏爱年度长约，但「现货市场」让所有人不敢乱来。

words.enDefinition: the cost of departmental unit

examples.en: The print shop quotes by departmental unit cost rather than gut feel.
examples.zh: 印刷车间的报价依据「部门单位成本」，而不是拍脑袋。

examples.en: Comparing departmental unit cost across plants exposed the aging press.
examples.zh: 对比各厂的「部门单位成本」，暴露出那台老印刷机的问题。

words.enDefinition: distribution of departmental secondary

examples.en: Departmental secondary distribution pushes service costs onto the producing workshops.
examples.zh: 「服务部门费用的第一次分配」把服务成本摊入生产车间。

examples.en: The textbook example walks through departmental secondary distribution with two service pools.
examples.zh: 教材用两个服务成本库的例子演示「服务部门费用的初次分配」。

words.enDefinition: revenue arising from departmental

examples.en: Afternoon tea drives a surprising share of departmental revenue at the hotel.
examples.zh: 下午茶为酒店贡献了相当可观的「分部门收入」。

examples.en: The dashboard breaks departmental revenue down by channel each morning.
examples.zh: 看板每天早上按渠道拆解「分部门收入」。

words.enDefinition: financial gain arising from departmental

examples.en: The board reviews departmental profit before setting next year's bonuses.
examples.zh: 董事会在设定明年奖金之前，会先审阅「部门利润」。

examples.en: Allocating head office rent changed every departmental profit line overnight.
examples.zh: 总部租金一摊入，各条「分部利润」一夜之间全变了样。

words.enDefinition: a system for departmental process cost

examples.en: Each workshop runs a departmental process cost system with its own normal loss.
examples.zh: 每个车间都执行「部门分步成本制」，各算各的正常损耗。

examples.en: Transfers between stages move at cost under the departmental process cost system.
examples.zh: 在「部门分步成本制」下，工序间转料按成本价计价。

collocations: test the departmental process cost system
refine the departmental process cost system
compare the departmental process cost system

words.enDefinition: amounts that must be paid or spent for fixed factory overhead

examples.en: Depreciation and plant security make up most of the fixed factory overhead costs.
examples.zh: 折旧和厂区安保构成「固定间接费用」的大头。

examples.en: Idle capacity keeps fixed factory overhead costs spread over fewer units.
examples.zh: 产能闲置使「固定间接费用」摊到更少的产品上。

words.enDefinition: fixed elements of costs used in professional practice

examples.en: The seminar separates the fixed elements of costs from truly variable ones.
examples.zh: 研讨课把「成本的固定部分」与真正的变动部分区分开来。

examples.en: Insurance premiums rank among the fixed elements of costs for the fleet.
examples.zh: 保费属于车队「成本中的固定部分」。

words.enDefinition: a split the cost used in professional practice

examples.en: The neighbors split the cost of the shared fence down the middle.
examples.zh: 两家人对半「分担」了共用围墙的费用。

examples.en: We agreed to split the cost of the trade fair booth three ways.
examples.zh: 我们商定三方「分摊」交易会展位费用。

words.enDefinition: describing something as informal in business contexts

examples.en: The dress code here is informal, so jeans are fine for client calls.
examples.zh: 这里的着装规范很「非正式」，见客户穿牛仔裤也没问题。

examples.en: Their agreement stayed informal until the first big order forced paperwork.
examples.zh: 他们的合作一直是「非正式的」，直到第一笔大单逼出了正式文件。

words.enDefinition: to continue firmly despite difficulty or opposition

examples.en: She persisted with the supplier even after two rejected prototypes.
examples.zh: 即使两版样品都被否决，她仍「坚持」与那家供应商合作。

examples.en: If the noise persists, maintenance will move us to another office.
